title: ground-loop-writes-its-own-liveness
intention: On each pass the ground loop writes a record in its own device space (~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/<instance>/) carrying: when it last ran, its state, and its pid. The write is part of the pass, not a separate concern.
why: The foundation the other three children read. It is also the first device record ever to reach disk in Cairn — the runtime-spine sweep measured ZERO. That makes it layer 0 of that sweep's map and this ticket at the same time: a scan-and-post loop that finds nothing produces no output, so without this record 'ran and found nothing' and 'never ran' are the same observation from outside.

falsifier.proves_red: The record's last-run does not advance while the loop runs, or advances while it does not. And: the record must survive being read mid-write (a reader must never see a torn record) — atomic write, same discipline as the projector's append door.
